definitions.explanation: A cutting technique where ingredients are sliced very thin (1-2mm). Used when you want ingredients to cook quickly, be tender, or have a delicate texture.

examples.japanese: {牛肉|ぎゅうにく}の{薄切|うすぎ}りですき{焼|や}きを{作|つく}る。
examples.english: Make sukiyaki with thinly sliced beef.

examples.japanese: しょうがを{薄切|うすぎ}りにする。
{薄切|うすぎ}り{肉|にく}は{火|ひ}が{通|とお}りやすい。
examples.english: Thinly sliced meat cooks through easily.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{薄|うす}い (thin) + {切|ぎ}り (cutting)

CUTTING TECHNIQUE:
Slice ingredients as thin as possible (1-2mm) using a sharp knife. Often used for meat that will be used in hot pot dishes or stir-fries.

COMMON INGREDIENTS:
- {牛肉|ぎゅうにく} - beef (for sukiyaki, shabu-shabu)
- {豚肉|ぶたにく} - pork
- しょうが - ginger
- にんにく - garlic
- きゅうり - cucumber

MEAT TERMINOLOGY:
{薄切|うすぎ}り{肉|にく} is sold specifically for:
- すき{焼|や}き - sukiyaki
- しゃぶしゃぶ - shabu-shabu
- {野菜|やさい}{炒|いた}め - vegetable stir-fry

COMMON PATTERN:
「〜を{薄切|うすぎ}りにする」 - to slice ~ thinly

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {薄切|うすぎ}り - thin slices
- {厚切|あつぎ}り - thick slices
